label: Mood
description: The emotional atmosphere a reader lives in, across the whole book or one part of it: the feeling that dominates, how hard it presses, where it shifts and what it leaves behind. Concrete details and sentence mechanics belong to other kinds.

fields.label: Dominant feeling
fields.help: The one feeling a reader should carry through most of the book, or of the part this mood covers, named as plainly as you can.

fields.label: Span covered
fields.help: How much of the book this mood governs, which decides which other moods it has to sit alongside.

fields.label: Undertone
fields.help: A second feeling that runs beneath the dominant one and colours it, if the mood carries one.

fields.label: What produces the feeling
fields.help: The story situations, pressures or uncertainties that produce the feeling, as distinct from the words and details on the page, one per item.

fields.label: Intensity
fields.help: How hard the dominant feeling presses on the reader across the span, from held well back to overwhelming.

fields.label: How the intensity moves
fields.help: The shape the intensity takes from the start of the span to its end.

fields.label: Weight of tone
fields.help: How far the mood leans towards gravity rather than lightness, counting how much humour it leaves room for.

fields.label: Reader beside the characters
fields.help: Whether the reader feels what the viewpoint characters feel, or something sooner, sharper or different that they cannot.

options.label: Feels it sooner or more than they do

fields.label: Opening feeling
fields.help: The feeling the first pages of the span set up, and how soon they arrive at the dominant feeling.

fields.label: Planned shifts
fields.help: The points where the feeling deliberately changes and what it changes to, one shift per item, in the order a reader meets them.

fields.label: Moments of relief
fields.help: Where and how the reader is briefly let off the pressure of the dominant feeling without the mood itself changing, one per item.

fields.label: Closing feeling
fields.help: The feeling a reader is left with on closing the book, or on leaving the part this mood covers.

fields.label: Tonal risks
fields.help: Ways this mood could misfire for a reader, such as numbing through sameness or tipping into excess, one per item, to test in later sessions.
